description: SIMPLIFIED 8-switch controller, not a full real sax key layout, but the 8 roles now match the actual hardware build confirmed against a real fingering chart (howtoplaysaxophone.org, checked 2026-08-22): an octave/register key (thumb) + 3 upper main keys (index/middle/ring, holes 1-3) + 3 lower main keys (index/middle/ring, holes 4-6) + the low C half-moon key (hole 7). This gives a clean 2-octave range with no cross-fingerings for chromatic notes -- side/palm keys and the second half-moon key are omitted given the 8-switch limit. FIXED 2026-08-22: earlier version of this file had the hole-covering direction backwards (more holes covered was mapped to a HIGHER pitch). Real woodwinds work the opposite way -- opening more holes shortens the effective tube and raises pitch, so covering more holes LOWERS it, matching how the trumpet's valves work conceptually (more engaged = lower). This file now reflects that: no holes covered = the highest note in the fingered octave, holes 1-6 all covered = the diatonic tonic, and adding hole 7 (low C key) on top of that extends one further diatonic step down to B3 -- a design choice for this simplified model, not a literal transcription of what the low C key does on a real horn. This extension is only used at the very bottom of the range (not mirrored into the upper octave), since the equivalent register+holes1-7 combination there would collide with B5's already-simpler open+register fingering. Chromatic (accidental) notes are still NOT resolvable with this simplified switch set -- the converter flags them as warnings.
